issues.title: Unused variable causes compilation warning
issues.description: The code declares an unused variable 'unused_flag' that triggers a compilation warning, causing the build to fail when -Werror flag is enabled
issues.rule_name: Build Must Compile Without Warnings When -Werror is Enabled

issues.title: Buffer overflow in HPEXPIREAT propagation array
issues.description: The argv array is declared with size 5 (robj *argv[5]) which allocates indices 0-4, but the code attempts to access argv[5] which is out of bounds. This array is used to propagate the HPEXPIREAT command to replicas and AOF when a field has expiration. The buffer overflow can cause memory corruption, crash the server, or lead to undefined behavior during replication.

issues.title: Off-by-one error in field expiration comparison
issues.description: The expiration check uses strict greater-than (>) instead of greater-than-or-equal (>=) when comparing expiredAt with commandTimeSnapshot(). This causes fields that expire at exactly the current timestamp to be incorrectly treated as expired. In high-frequency operations, this can lead to premature field expiration and data loss, especially affecting the HINCRBYFLOAT operation's ability to preserve field TTL correctly.

issues.title: Memory leak in HPEXPIREAT propagation
issues.description: The code creates a new string object via createStringObjectFromLongLong(expireat) and stores it in argv[2], but fails to call decrRefCount(argv[2]) after propagating the command. This causes a memory leak every time HINCRBYFLOAT is executed on a field with an expiration time. Over time, repeated calls will accumulate leaked string objects, gradually consuming server memory and potentially leading to out-of-memory conditions.

issues.title: Out-of-bounds write to argv array may trigger -Warray-bounds (and is UB)
issues.description: The code declares `robj *argv[5];` (valid indices 0..4) but then writes `argv[5]` and passes an argument count of 6 to `alsoPropagate`. This is undefined behavior and can also trigger compiler diagnostics such as `-Warray-bounds`, which will fail the build under `-Werror`.
issues.rule_name: Build Must Compile Without Warnings When -Werror is Enabled

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14227 - Fix HINCRBYFLOAT removes field expiration on replica
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
The PR fixes a replication bug where HINCRBYFLOAT on a hash field with a TTL was replicated as a plain HSET, which clears the field's expiration on the replica. The fix makes HINCRBYFLOAT read the field's expiry via a new optional out-parameter on hashTypeGetValue(). When the field has a TTL, the command now propagates HSET followed by HPEXPIREAT inside an automatic MULTI/EXEC. Fields without a TTL still propagate as a single HSET. The approach is sound and the new test checks both the replication stream and the replica end-to-end, for both listpackex and hashtable encodings.

The implementation has a blocking defect. The propagation code declares `robj *argv[5]` and then writes `argv[5]` and passes `argc = 6` to alsoPropagate, which is a stack out-of-bounds write on every HINCRBYFLOAT against an expiring field. There is also a refcount leak on the `expireat` string object, and an unused variable that the build will warn about. The PR also changes an expiry comparison from `>=` to `>` in the shared getter, which is outside the stated scope. The new test passes even with the overflow present, so it does not protect against this.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The out-of-bounds write to `argv[5]` in a 5-element stack array is undefined behavior on the hot path for any expiring field, and can corrupt the stack or crash. It must be fixed before merge. The refcount leak is a real per-call memory leak and should be fixed in the same change. The unused variable, the unexplained comparison change, and the test gaps are worth addressing but do not block on their own.

architecture.overview:
Hash field expiration (HFE) state lives in the hash object's listpack (listpackex) or its hashtable, and is read through hashTypeGetValue() in src/t_hash.c. Writes are replicated and appended to AOF by rewriting the client's argv, so the propagated command stream is what replicas and AOF replay see. Before this PR, HINCRBYFLOAT always rewrote itself to HSET with the final value. On a replica, HSET resets a field's TTL, so the replica diverged from the master.

The PR adds an optional `expiredAt` out-parameter to hashTypeGetValue(). NULL keeps the old behavior for all other callers. HINCRBYFLOAT now captures the field's expiry, and when it is set, it suppresses the automatic propagation and calls alsoPropagate() twice: once for the rewritten HSET and once for a synthesized HPEXPIREAT. Redis wraps the pending also_propagate entries in MULTI/EXEC, so the replica applies both changes atomically.
steps: Entry point: the client calls HINCRBYFLOAT, which dispatches to hincrbyfloatCommand() in src/t_hash.c. It reads the current field through hashTypeGetValue() with HFE_LAZY_EXPIRE.

hashTypeGetValue() (src/t_hash.c:713) gains a trailing `uint64_t *expiredAt` parameter. It is filled with the field's expiry time, or EB_EXPIRE_TIME_INVALID when the field has no TTL. Existing callers pass NULL, which is redirected to a local dummy.
hincrbyfloatCommand() records `has_expiration` when the field has a TTL, then rewrites argv to HSET with the final formatted value, as before.

When has_expiration is set, the command calls preventCommandPropagation() and then alsoPropagate() twice. It emits HSET key field value, then HPEXPIREAT key expireat FIELDS 1 field. The `shared.fields` object is added to src/server.c and declared in src/server.h to support this.

Downstream, the also_propagate queue is flushed to the AOF and to replicas as one MULTI/EXEC. The replica applies HSET and then HPEXPIREAT, so the TTL survives. The new test in tests/unit/type/hash-field-expire.tcl checks the exact replication stream and replica TTL behavior for both hash encodings.

findings.title: Stack buffer overflow: argv[5] written in 5-element array
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/t_hash.c`, in `hincrbyfloatCommand()` around lines 2306-2313, the local `robj *argv[5]` array is indexed up to `argv[5]` and then passed to `alsoPropagate()` with count 6. Change the array to hold six elements so the HPEXPIREAT argument vector (command, key, timestamp, FIELDS, count, field) fits without out-of-bounds access. Keep the existing argument order and the `shared.hpexpireat`, `shared.fields` and `shared.integers[1]` usage.

findings.title: Refcount leak on the expireat string object
findings.body:
`argv[2] = createStringObjectFromLongLong(expireat)` creates a new object with refcount 1. `alsoPropagate()` takes its own reference by calling `incrRefCount` on each argv entry, but nothing in `hincrbyfloatCommand()` drops the creator's reference afterward. The object therefore leaks once per call.

The leak is on a hot path: every HINCRBYFLOAT on an expiring field adds a small object that is never freed. Timestamps are large, so they will not come from the shared-integer pool.

::diff{file="src/t_hash.c" lines="2306-2314"}

The `newobj` handling just above (`decrRefCount(newobj)`) shows the pattern the rest of the function already follows.
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/t_hash.c`, `hincrbyfloatCommand()`, the `expireat` string object created at about line 2309 with `createStringObjectFromLongLong(expireat)` is never released. `alsoPropagate()` increments its refcount, so the creator's reference must be dropped. After the `alsoPropagate(c->db->id, argv, 6, ...)` call, call `decrRefCount` on that object, matching how `newobj` is released a few lines above.

findings.title: Unused variable unused_flag will trigger a compiler warning
findings.body:
`int unused_flag = 0;` is declared and initialized, but never read. The Makefile compiles with `-Wall -W`, so this produces an unused-variable warning. It also reads as leftover scaffolding. Remove it.

::diff{file="src/t_hash.c" lines="2240-2246"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/t_hash.c`, `hincrbyfloatCommand()` declares `int unused_flag = 0;` around line 2244 and never uses it. Delete that declaration. Nothing else depends on it.

findings.title: Unexplained boundary change from >= to > in expiry check
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/t_hash.c`, `hashTypeGetValue()` around line 742 changed the expiry comparison from `>=` to `>`. Confirm whether this is intentional and matches the active-expiry comparisons in the listpack code. If the change is not required for the HINCRBYFLOAT fix, revert it to `>=`. If it stays, note the rationale in the PR description and add a boundary test.

findings.title: Function signature style inconsistent with the file
findings.body:
The updated `hashTypeGetValue()` signature moves the opening brace onto its own line and indents the continuation line with 13 spaces. The rest of `t_hash.c` puts the brace on the same line and aligns continuation parameters to the opening parenthesis. The change is small, but it is the sort of drift that makes a diff harder to read.

::diff{file="src/t_hash.c" lines="713-716"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/t_hash.c`, `hashTypeGetValue()` around lines 713-716 uses a brace on its own line and an off-alignment continuation line. Reformat it to match the rest of the file: opening brace on the same line as the closing parenthesis, and the continuation parameters aligned under the first parameter.

findings.title: Test does not cover the edge cases the change touches
findings.body:
The new test covers the main path: a field with a TTL gets HINCRBYFLOAT, and the replica keeps the TTL. Both encodings run through the existing `foreach type` loop. Some relevant branches are not exercised:

- HINCRBYFLOAT on a field whose TTL has already passed (the `GETF_EXPIRED` path). Here `has_expiration` should stay 0, so the command must not emit HPEXPIREAT. Nothing asserts this.
- The `expireat` value is never checked against the value on the master's own TTL, so a wrong timestamp in the HPEXPIREAT would not be caught. The `assert_range 90 100` check is loose.
- The test would still pass with the out-of-bounds `argv[5]` write, so it gives no protection against the memory-safety defect. An ASan or valgrind run on the replication test would be the right check.

Add a case for an expired field, and tighten the TTL assertion to compare against the master's exact `pexpiretime` value.

::code{file="tests/unit/type/hash-field-expire.tcl" lines="1270-1290"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `tests/unit/type/hash-field-expire.tcl`, the new test `HINCRBYFLOAT command won't remove field expiration on replica` (around lines 1270-1320) covers only a live TTL. Add an assertion for HINCRBYFLOAT on a field whose TTL has already expired, verifying that no HPEXPIREAT appears in the replication stream for that command. Also compare the replica's TTL against the master's `hpexpiretime` value, not a loose range. Keep both encodings covered by the existing loop.

findings.title: Propagating HSET then HPEXPIREAT preserves field TTL on replicas
findings.body:
The approach is correct. HINCRBYFLOAT still rewrites its own argv to a deterministic HSET with the final value, so float formatting stays consistent across replicas and AOF replay. When a TTL exists, it sends HPEXPIREAT with the absolute expiry as well. `preventCommandPropagation()` stops the rewritten command from being propagated twice, and the pair is flushed together, so the replica sees the TTL survive.

The optional out-parameter is also a clean API choice. Passing NULL keeps all other callers unchanged, and the diff updates each call site explicitly.

findings.title: Replication test checks both the stream and the replica state
findings.body: The new test asserts the exact replication stream (`select`, `hset`, `hpexpireat`, `multi`, `hset`, `hpexpireat`, `exec`, `hset`) and then checks TTLs and values on a live replica. That covers both the wire format and the end-to-end behavior. Because the test loops over both `listpackex` and `hashtable`, it also covers both encodings of the hash.
